q: The concept of ____ is very important for the physical and biological sciences.
e: The concept of temperature is very important for the physical and biological sciences. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: This is because the ____ of an object is directly related to the energies of molecules composing the object.
e: This is because the temperature of an object is directly related to the energies of molecules composing the object. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: Natural processes often involve energy changes and the ____ is an indicator for these changes.
e: Natural processes often involve energy changes and the temperature is an indicator for these changes. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: It is expected that students will identify that thermal energy is an ____ of a matter.
e: It is expected that students will identify that thermal energy is an internal energy of a matter. Internal energy here means the capacity to do work.

q: The sensations of hotness, warmness and coldness can be experienced by ____ objects.
e: The sensations of hotness, warmness and coldness can be experienced by touching objects. The physics in this sentence is built around touching.

q: ____ is the quantity that determines how cold (or) how hot the object is.
e: Temperature is the quantity that determines how cold (or) how hot the object is. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: To measure temperature accurately, we use instruments called ____.
e: To measure temperature accurately, we use instruments called thermometers. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The energy exchanged between an object and its surrounding due to different temperatures is defined as ____.
e: The energy exchanged between an object and its surrounding due to different temperatures is defined as heat. Heat here means energy that flows because of a temperature difference. Heat is energy on the move; it is not the same word as temperature.

q: The unit of heat is the same as units of ____.
e: The unit of heat is the same as units of energy. Energy here means the capacity to do work. Heat is energy on the move; it is not the same word as temperature.

q: When a body at a higher temperature is in contact with a body at a lower temperature, ____ flows from the first to the second body.
e: When a body at a higher temperature is in contact with a body at a lower temperature, heat flows from the first to the second body. Heat here means energy that flows because of a temperature difference. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The motions and positions of molecules in matter result in the ____ energy and potential energy.
e: The motions and positions of molecules in matter result in the kinetic energy and potential energy. Kinetic here means energy a body has because it is moving. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

q: The total energy, that is, the sum of the potential energy and the kinetic energy, of molecules in matter is in fact the ____ of that matter.
e: The total energy, that is, the sum of the potential energy and the kinetic energy, of molecules in matter is in fact the internal energy of that matter. Internal energy here means the capacity to do work. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

q: Temperature is a measure of the ____ of molecules.
e: Temperature is a measure of the internal energy of molecules. Internal energy here means the capacity to do work. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.
